conflict_rule: AI systems must comply with all Commonwealth IT Policies, Management Directives and other applicable regulations (5.1.9); exceptions only via the IT Policy Governance Process (s.7).

record_provenance.notes: Text taken from the copy in asago-ai/asago-policy-mapper (policy_examples/penn.pdf). The asago file name 'penn' refers to the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania (state government), not the University of Pennsylvania. No official URL or ITP number is printed in the document (PDF metadata: pa.gov author, created 20 Jan 2026). Current version effective 13 Jan 2026, scheduled review January 2027; contents of earlier versions are known only from the revision history. Mandatory for agencies, their users and third-party vendors/contractors as an executive-branch IT policy, but not legislation (binding=false). The document refers to the NIST AI RMF as 'currently being developed' with an initial draft, which is outdated text.

clauses.original_text: Agencies shall ensure that AI solutions have appropriate interventions and checks from humans, otherwise known as human in the loop (HITL) procedures, meaning there is active human participation in the decision-making process, review, oversight, and validation of AI systems including any generated content or output.
clauses.object: human-in-the-loop interventions and checks on AI solutions
clauses.requirement: HITL procedures for AI decision-making, review, oversight and validation
clauses.condition: before agencies begin an AI initiative (key consideration)
clauses.purpose: maintain human control over AI-assisted decisions and outputs
clauses.affected_asset: Commonwealth decisions; citizens and employees affected
clauses.applicable_systems: AI solutions and generative AI tools used by Commonwealth agencies
clauses.interpretation_notes: Listed among key considerations agencies 'shall evaluate' before starting an AI initiative.

clauses.original_text: Evaluate the level of risk that AI systems are exploited by malicious actors and determine appropriate risk controls. Establish controls to prevent adversarial learning to include attacks that try to influence the training data of spam filters or systems for abnormal network traffic detection, designed to mislead the learning algorithm for subsequent exploitation.
clauses.object: exploitation of AI systems and adversarial learning
clauses.requirement: assess exploitation risk and implement controls against adversarial attacks
clauses.purpose: secure AI systems against malicious actors
clauses.applicable_systems: AI solutions and generative AI tools used by Commonwealth agencies
clauses.interpretation_notes: Introduced by 'the following shall be considered for use', so modality recorded as SHOULD. Bullets joined.

clauses.original_text: When using any Generative AI for Commonwealth business purposes, the user is accountable for any Generative AI outputs and must review and verify all associated output content.
clauses.requirement: users are accountable for and must verify all GenAI output
clauses.condition: when using GenAI for Commonwealth business purposes
clauses.interpretation_notes: The section adds that users must have experience in the relevant topic area to verify outputs, and lists bias, dated or inaccurate information, hallucinations, inappropriate content, IP and confidential information as review points.

clauses.original_text: Users shall be transparent about their use of generative AI and must disclose to customers, residents, visitors, and industry when generative AI has been used to generate content that may be public facing or shared externally. Generative AI use must be disclosed even if it was only used to generate a portion of the content. The disclosure shall be prominently displayed and include an indication that the content was generated either entirely or in part by generative AI and identify the Generative AI system and version that was used.
clauses.object: use of generative AI in public-facing or externally shared content
clauses.requirement: prominent disclosure naming the GenAI system and version
clauses.condition: content that may be public facing or shared externally
clauses.affected_asset: public trust; recipients of Commonwealth content
clauses.interpretation_notes: Example given: 'ChatGPT-3.5 was used in the creation of this document.' Section 5.1.5 separately requires AI solutions to disclose to customers that they are interacting with AI.

clauses.original_text: No class C data, as defined in the Data Classification Policy, may be input into any generative AI prompt, tool, or system. This includes, but is not limited to: Sensitive Security Information; Personal Identifiable Information (PII); Protected Health Information (PHI); … Confidential or Non-Public Information; Privileged Information; Prerequisite-Required Information
clauses.object: class C data (SSI, PII, PHI, regulated, confidential, privileged data)
clauses.recipient: generative AI prompts, tools or systems
clauses.requirement: no class C data in any generative AI tool
clauses.purpose: protect sensitive, personal and regulated data
clauses.affected_asset: personal data; PHI; regulated data (SSA, IRS, CMS, CJI, CHRIA, FERPA, PCI DSS)
clauses.applicable_systems: any generative AI prompt, tool, or system
clauses.interpretation_notes: Bulleted list flattened with semicolons; the regulated-data sub-list is elided. Non-public records exempt under the Right-to-Know Law (65 P.S. §§ 67.101 et seq.) are also excluded.

clauses.original_text: Generative AI outputs are not to be used to make decisions for or on behalf of employees. Employees may use generative AI outputs to inform a larger decision-making process, but ultimately the Commonwealth employee or official remains the final decision maker. … Generative AI cannot make reliable subjective or value-based judgments and may not be used for such purposes.
clauses.action: not use GenAI outputs to make
clauses.requirement: GenAI informs but never makes decisions; a human remains the final decision maker
clauses.exception: GenAI outputs may inform a larger human decision-making process
clauses.affected_asset: employees and citizens affected by decisions
clauses.interpretation_notes: Example in source: 'do not use generative AI to make final decisions that affect employment.'
